summary: Iteration 4 tested all NEW features (campaigns + reference URLs/images + article preview/txt export). Backend: 10/10 pytest cases pass (list/get campaigns, 404, update persistence, export markdown/txt/html, invalid format 400, unknown id 404, article txt export). Frontend: verified Dashboard title 'Content Studio', articles/campaigns tabs with counts, ?tab=campaigns query param, ReferenceInputs (URL add + image thumbnail) work on both /campaigns/new and /generate. CampaignEditor for existing campaign fc7229ca... showed post cards for facebook/tiktok/email with content, hashtags, copy, download buttons; text edit persisted after save+reload; export dialog rendered txt/markdown/html buttons and campaign-export-txt-button triggered a .txt download (chill-out-organic-cold-brew-launch.txt); download-post-facebook also triggered a .txt download. Generated exactly ONE new article via UI with Wikipedia URL reference + PNG upload; navigation to /editor/{id} succeeded (~60-90s); preview-tab rendered 11 headings and 1 whose src is the public /api/files/... URL with descriptive alt text 'Cold brew coffee preparation with dark red background showing rich coffee tones'; backend GET /api/articles/{id} returned reference_urls=[wiki URL] and image_paths length=1 and content contained markdown image referencing the uploaded file; article export-txt-button triggered .txt download. Delete-campaign flow: delete-campaign-button opened AlertDialog, confirm-delete-button removed the card and displayed 'Campaign deleted' toast + empty-state.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: /api/campaigns/{id}/export error message text says "Use 'markdown', 'txt' or 'html'" which is correct; article export error still says "Use 'markdown' or 'html'" even though 'txt' is now supported — update the article export 400 message for parity.
PUT /api/campaigns/{id} does not validate that provided platforms in posts match campaign.platforms; not blocking but consider a light check.
CampaignGenerator page shows 6 platform checkboxes but backend PLATFORMS excludes 'email' (email is a separate include_email flag) — current behavior is correct; just noting for maintainers.
